result:
`./compile.sh` reports `compiled OK`.

I created `tests/org/apache/commons/csv/CSVPrinterAgentTest.java`, a self-contained JUnit 5 test class covering:

- Constructor contract: null `Appendable`/`CSVFormat` → `NullPointerException`; hybrid encapsulation+escaping format → `IllegalArgumentException`; header written immediately (and `IOException` propagated if the stream fails during that write).
- `getOut()` identity, `getRecordCount()` starting at 0 and excluding comments/headers.
- `print`/`println` behavior (no separator vs. separator-only).
- `printRecord` (array, `Iterable`, `Stream`) — quoting on delimiter/quote chars, record separator, record count increment, zero-arg record, `IOException` propagation.
- `printRecords` (array, `Iterable`, `Stream`) — simple values as one record vs. nested arrays/collections as multiple records.
- `printComment` — no-op when comments are disabled, marker+space formatting, splitting on embedded line breaks, and starting a fresh line when content is pending.
- `flush()`/`close()`/`close(boolean)` — verified via a counting `Writer` fixture.
- `printHeaders(ResultSet)`, `printRecords(ResultSet)`, and `printRecords(ResultSet, boolean)` — verified via a `java.lang.reflect.Proxy`-based fake `ResultSet`/`ResultSetMetaData` (since `java.sql.ResultSet` isn't in `api/`, a proxy avoids needing to decompile anything to stub the full interface).

All expectations trace back to the documented contract in `api/org/apache/commons/csv/CSVPrinter.html`; `CSVFormat` is only used as unavoidable fixture scaffolding, built explicitly in each test rather than relying on undocumented defaults.
